subject: Orion Logistics — isolation & on-prem qualification recap
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@orionlogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 13:02:00 -0500
Subject: Recap: Isolation, air-gap drivers, and next steps (call today)

Hi Maria — thanks again for taking the call today. This thread captures the short recap, the constraints you shared, and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track items before we bring in our solutions team.

Goal you stated
- Move to a private hosting option (VPC or on-prem) to satisfy regulatory requirements and in-house encryption controls while preserving low-latency inference for regional hubs.

Top pain points
- Strict data residency: certain PII/manifest data must remain in-app in US-East physical region and cannot leave the corporate VPC.
- Network isolation: some sites require an air-gapped pattern for model inference (no inbound internet), with occasional batched outbound uploads to secure sftp.
- KMS control: keys must be customer-managed (HSM/KMS) & rotate per policy; Redwood-managed keys are not acceptable for the workload in scope.
- Minimal changes to existing firewall/NAT strategy: IT does not want to open broad inbound ports or change routing model for edge locations.

Summary of options we discussed
1) Private deployment (customer VPC, Redwood control plane in a partner region) — gives you the private runtime inside your VPC with minimal egress; requires static outbound IPs for allowlisting and VPC peering/VPN for control plane telemetry.
2) On-prem air-gap variant — full offline runtime inside your datacenter, periodic manual artifact sync (signed container images) and a local control console. This addresses the strictest air-gap requests but adds operational cadence on your side.

Immediate asks from Orion (from call)
- Network sketch of how hub sites currently route to outbound proxies and SFTP gateways (we asked Maria to share).
- Confirmation of which data types are in-scope for residency (PII vs telemetry).
- Preferred KMS vendor and whether HSM-backed keys are required.

Attached: rough checklist from our side to speed qualification (redwood_private_deploy_checklist.xlsx) and a blank SOC2 scoping questionnaire for your security team (soc2_scope_questionnaire.docx). I also included a quick sketch placeholder for the network diagram — if you can drop your diagram in the drive link, we’ll annotate.

Next steps and owners
- Maria: share network diagram and a short list of data classes by Wed 2027-01-20.
- Priyom: follow up with configuration matrix and estimated timeline for dedicated/private options by Thu 2027-01-21.
- Marissa/Ben: stand by for a technical deep-dive once we receive diagrams.

If any of the above is off, correct me here. I’ll loop in the solutions engineers once Maria confirms the diagram and data scope.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0194

From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@orionlogistics.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ashley Kim <ashley.kim@orionlogistics.com>, it@orionlogistics.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 16:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Recap: Isolation, air-gap drivers, and next steps (call today)

Thanks, Priyom — clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Data classes: the critical set is shipment manifests + customer-identifying PII. Telemetry (metrics, model traces) can be exported out with a pseudonymization step, but manifests must reside in our environment.
- KMS: we use AWS KMS with CloudHSM backing in our production AWS accounts. We require a solution that integrates with our KMS to perform envelope encryption; Redwood managing keys is not acceptable.
- Network: most sites are behind an outbound-only proxy; there is no path for inbound connections except through our bastion for management. Edge inference nodes must initiate connections outbound to an allowlisted set of IPs.
- Air-gap: only two of our five highest-risk sites need a full air-gap pattern; the rest can be handled with private VPC hosting.

I attached a redlined network sketch (very rough) and a short answers doc from our security team. We will not be able to permit inbound control-plane webhooks to edge sites.

We can target Wed 2027-01-20 for the diagram and data scope confirmation. Procurement will likely ask for a high-level MSA and an estimated monthly cost range before we proceed to the engineering deep-dive.

Regards,
Maria Garcia
IT Lead, Orion Logistics
maria.garcia@orionlogistics.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@orionlogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@orionlogistics.com
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Recap: Isolation, air-gap drivers, and next steps (call today)

Hi Maria — appreciate the quick clarifications and the sketch. Two quick operational notes and an ask: 

Operational notes
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS and can plug into AWS KMS with CloudHSM-backed keys for envelope encryption; we will need an IAM role + key access policy from your side for the initial setup.
- Outbound-only model: our private runtime can be configured to use static outbound IPs and operate behind your proxies; control-plane telemetry can be batched and forwarded to your SFTP gateway if you prefer no direct connections.

Ask
- Can you confirm which two sites require full air-gap? Names or site IDs are fine. That will let us scope the on-prem variant and estimate uplift.

Proposed immediate deliverables
1) Priyom: a short configuration matrix (VPC vs on-prem) showing firewall rules, required ports, and KMS integration steps (deliver by Thu 2027-01-21).
2) Marissa: technical checklist + an optional template runbook for the on-prem image sync (deliver by Fri 2027-01-22).
3) Ben: cost ballpark for both options including uplift for air-gapped sites (deliver by Fri 2027-01-22).

If that timeline looks tight on your end, let me know and we can extend by a week. I’ll also prepare a short pre-sales MSA summary we can share with Procurement to speed approvals.

Best,
Priyom

Note: forwarded to procurement to keep them in the loop for timing and MSA expectations.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Internal: cost sketch and questions for Orion

Internal notes (not to send to customer yet) — drafting cost approach and open questions.

Cost sketch assumptions
- VPC private runtime per region: baseline $Xk/month (includes runtime, monitoring, 99th-percentile token SLA).
- On-prem air-gap: one-time deployment fee + image sync service + manual support windows. Expect uplift of ~2.5x for fully air-gapped site due to integration and patch cadence.

Open technical questions to confirm with Maria before sending numbers
- Do the air-gapped sites have local HSM appliances or will they accept software KMS with a customer-managed key?
- For outbound proxies, can Orion provide a static NAT mapping per site, or do we need to support a dynamic agent that can register IPs?
- Is there a preferred cadence for batched telemetry uploads (daily vs weekly)?

Planned next internal steps
- Marissa to draft runbook template by EOD Fri and capture the exact firewall rules we will request.
- Priyom to finalize configuration matrix; I’ll align on cost ranges after that.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
